q: Which earlier document was superseded by UAP-IAPOA Doc. 210?
n: Doc. 210 formally supersedes the older 1979 fee guideline, updating it to the post-R.A. 9266 regulatory framework.

q: Doc. 210 was issued to comply with which PRBoA issuance?
n: The Guidelines were prescribed under PRBoA Resolution No. 3, s. 2010; a later Resolution No. 6, s. 2016 merely published it in the Official Gazette.

q: Under a DAEDS contract, what share of the total fee is attributed to architectural design services specifically?
n: Since architectural design is the core scope, it makes up 60% of the full DAEDS fee, with engineering/allied services making up the rest — this is also why DADS rates are 60% of DAEDS rates.

q: Which basis, used in the % of PCC method, is described by the abbreviation "PPCC"?
o: Probable Project Construction Cost, fixed at signing
n: PPCC is a mutually-agreed estimate using unit-price parameters (market rate/sqm) fixed at signing — distinct from the Awarded (bid-based) or Final (cost-records-based) PCC.

q: In the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense method, what range does the multiplier (M) usually fall within?
n: The multiplier compensates for overhead, benefits, contingencies, capital interest, and profit; it typically falls between 1.5 and 2.5 depending on office set-up and complexity.
ref: UAP-IAPOA Doc. 210, Sec. 4, 4.3.8; Annex A, Multiplier

q: What acceptance fee, based on the agreed Professional Fee, should the Architect request upon signing for Pre-Design Services?
n: The 5% acceptance fee secures the engagement before pre-design work begins and is credited against the agreed Professional Fee.

q: For a Group 1 building (e.g., a warehouse) with a PCC of ₱50.0M or less, what DAEDS Recommended Professional Fee applies?
n: Group 1 covers the simplest building types (warehouses, garages, industrial plants), so it carries the lowest base rate among the groups at 5% for PCC up to P50M.

q: Given a Group 1 building with a PCC of ₱80,000,000, and using the DAEDS bracket of ₱2,500,000 plus 4% of the excess over ₱50.0M, what is the resulting Professional Fee?
n: Excess over P50M = P30M; 4% × P30M = P1,200,000; add the P2,500,000 base for the bracket to get P3,700,000.
ref: UAP-IAPOA Doc. 210, Sec. 6.3, Group 1 DAEDS table
steps: 4% × P30M = P1,200,000; add the P2,500,000 base for the bracket to get P3,700,000.

q: What DAEDS Recommended Professional Fee applies to Group 4 (single-detached residences, duplexes, row-houses, small apartments/townhouses)?
n: Residential work (Group 4) is compensated at a flat 10% of PCC for DAEDS, higher than Groups 1--3 since it isn't bracketed by cost.

q: Group 5, which covers monumental buildings (museums, memorials, expo/fair buildings), carries what DAEDS RPF?
n: Group 5 (monumental/highly decorative buildings) demands the most consummate design skill of the flat-rate groups, so it carries a 12% DAEDS rate versus 10% for ordinary residences.

q: Under Group 6 (repetitive construction, where the same plan is reused unamended), what RPF is charged for the third building in the series?
n: The scale steps down with each repeat build (100% → 50% → 40% → 30%) since design effort is already spent; the 3rd building falls at 40%.

q: Under Group 7 (Housing Project, DAEDS), how is the fee computed for units 2 through 10?
o: 10% of PCC per unit, with no reduction
The fee for one unit, plus 50% of RPF for each additional unit
The fee for one unit, plus 40% of RPF for each additional unit
A flat 6% of PCC no matter how many units
n: The first unit is billed at the full 10% DAEDS rate; each additional unit from the 2nd--10th adds only 50% of that RPF, reflecting reduced design effort per repeat unit.

q: Group 8 — extensive detail work such as built-in components, architectural interiors, and development planning/design — carries what flat RPF?
n: Group 8 covers highly detailed interior/built-in work, warranting the highest flat rate among the building-type groups at 15% of PCC.

q: How is compensation determined for Group 9 (alterations, renovations, and retrofits to existing Group 1–5 buildings)?
o: It is cut by 50% of the applicable RPF
It is increased by 50%, for a total of 150% of the applicable RPF
It is fixed at 12% of PCC regardless of the building's group
It is charged at the Group 8 rate of 15%
n: Renovation/retrofit work requires more effort per unit of construction cost than new construction, so the applicable RPF (from Groups 1--5) is surcharged by 50%.

q: Under Group 10 (rendering opinion/advice on technical matters), what is the minimum chargeable RPF?
n: This is a floor rate for consultation/opinion work — P1,000/hour minimum, rising with the scope and location of the engagement.

q: Under the standard payment schedule, what CUMULATIVE percentage of the Professional Fee is owed once Design Development Services are complete?
n: Cumulative payments build up: 5% at signing, +15% at Schematic Design = 20%, +20% at Design Development = 40% cumulative.

q: What CUMULATIVE percentage of the Professional Fee falls due upon completing the Contract Documents phase?
n: The Contract Documents phase is the largest single billing (50% of PF), bringing the running total from 40% to 90% cumulative — only the 10% Construction-completion payment remains.

q: If the Construction Phase is suspended for longer than six months, what becomes of the fee owed for the remaining Periodic Construction Supervision work?
n: A long suspension (over 6 months) disrupts the Architect's workflow and staffing, so the remaining periodic supervision fee is doubled to compensate for the disruption.

q: What Recommended Professional Fee applies to Full-Time Construction Supervision Services under SPP Doc. 204-A?
n: Full-time supervision is a dedicated on-site role, priced as a modest percentage band (1--1.5%) of PCC, separate from and additional to the design fee.

q: What Recommended Professional Fee applies to Construction Management Services under SPP Doc. 204-B?
n: Construction Management carries broader managerial responsibility than plain supervision, so its RPF band (1.5--3%) is higher than the 1--1.5% for Full-Time Supervision.

q: When acting as Building Administrator under Post-Construction Services (SPP Doc. 205), how is the RPF expressed?
n: Post-construction building administration is compensated as value-pricing tied to revenue generated, not to construction cost — hence the fee is a % of gross rental, not of PCC.

q: Serving as overall Project Manager under Comprehensive Architectural Services (SPP Doc. 206), what RPF does the Architect earn?
n: As overall Project/Development Manager overseeing a multidisciplinary team, the Architect earns 2--5% of PCC for that PM role, separate from any Regular Design Services fee on the same project.

q: What RPF applies to Design-Build Services by Administration under SPP Doc. 207?
n: Design-Build by Administration bundles construction-phase responsibility onto the Architect, billed at 7% of PCC on top of (exclusive of) the Regular Design Services fee.

q: What RPF applies to Design-Build Services on a Guaranteed Maximum Cost basis?
o: 10% of PCC, or built into the Guaranteed Maximum Cost
n: Taking on cost-overrun risk under a Guaranteed Maximum Cost commands a higher rate than Administration mode — 10% of PCC, or it may instead be built directly into the GMC figure.

q: For Physical Planning / Site Development Planning (SPP Doc. 203), what RPF applies to the first five hectares or less?
n: P50,000/ha equates to P5.00/sqm net to the Architect for the first 5 hectares, before the rate steps down for larger areas.

q: If the Owner directly and separately engages Specialist Consultants under Specialized Architectural Services, what coordination fee does the Architect receive?
n: When the Owner engages SCs directly (bypassing the Architect), the Architect still coordinates their input and is paid 5% of the SC's fee for that coordination role — the same principle recurs under Secs. 8.5 and 9.5.

q: Under Sec. 16, on what basis is interest computed when a fee remains unpaid more than 30 days after billing?
o: The prevailing rate set by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP)
The Client's own bank lending rate
No interest can ever be charged
n: Rather than a fixed statutory rate, the interest rate floats with the BSP's prevailing rate, as mutually agreed by Architect and Client, once billing is over 30 days unpaid.

q: Per Sec. 19, which body handles Service Agreement disputes that escalate to arbitration?
o: The Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture (PRBoA)
The Department of Trade and Industry (DTI)
n: Under R.A. 9285 and E.O. 1000, unresolved disputes escalate to CIAC arbitration (after negotiation/mediation fail), with CIAC bound to resolve within six months.

q: Under Annex A, the fee basis "Cost of Work (CoW)" applies specifically to which type of service?
n: "Cost of Work" is a defined term specific to Specialized Architectural Services (interiors, acoustics, lighting, site works, landscaping), used as the fee base instead of PCC.
ref: UAP-IAPOA Doc. 210, Annex A, Cost of Work

q: What does the abbreviation "RPF" stand for in the UAP fee guidelines?
n: RPF is the reference/benchmark fee the Guidelines set for each building type and service, factoring in scope and adjustment factors.
ref: UAP-IAPOA Doc. 210, Annex A, xviii; Annex B

q: Following the Sec. 4.1.2 worked example — a high-rise office of 10,000 sqm GFA at ₱30,000/sqm historical PCC, a 6% PCC fee, plus 2,000 sqm of non-GFA area billed at 50% of the GFA rate — what is the GFA portion of the fee alone?
n: GFA fee = unit PCC × fee rate × area = P30,000 × 0.06 × 10,000 sqm = P18,000,000; the non-GFA portion is computed separately and added on top.

q: For the Sorsogon Medical Center (Building Group 3, Annex D), after layering the Level 1 Specialist, BIM, new-construction-technology, third-party certification, DOH approval, multiple-bid, and other adjustment factors onto the 7.0% DAEDS base, what does the adjusted sub-total fee rate come to?
n: Adjustment factors (Level 1 Specialist 0.50 + BIM 0.10 + new tech 0.10 + certification 0.10 + DOH approval 0.10 + multiple bids 0.25 = 1.05%) are added to the 7.0% base to reach an 8.05% sub-total, which then drives the bracketed peso computation.
ref: UAP-IAPOA Doc. 210, Annex D — DAEDS Worksheet

q: Per Sec. 3, on which factors is compensation mutually evaluated?
o: Talent, skill, experience, effort, and time the project demands
The size of the Architect's firm
n: Compensation isn't just a mechanical % — it reflects the Architect's talents, skill, experience, effort, and the time the project demands.

q: Per Sec. 3.1, what should the compensation method allow the Client to do?
o: Delay payment until the project is finished
Avoid disclosing how the fee was computed
n: One of the three core aims of the compensation method (per 3.1) is that the Client be able to know costs in advance, alongside being commensurate with services and reflecting value.

q: Per Sec. 4.2.1, when is the Lump Sum or Fixed Fee method generally appropriate?
o: When the project scope is uncertain or still evolving
When the scope of services can already be clearly and fully defined at the outset
Only for interim or short-term engagements
n: Lump Sum/Fixed Fee requires the scope to be fully known upfront so the Architect can prepare an accurate work-hour and overhead estimate before quoting a single figure.

q: Per Sec. 4.2.2, which two approaches are generally used to arrive at a lump-sum figure?
o: A government-fixed table and a Client-imposed cap
A percentage of PPCC, and a direct build-up of cost-outline elements plus profit
Hourly billing and per diem rates
n: The two approaches — a percentage-of-cost shortcut and a bottom-up cost-outline build-up — are often used together, each checking the other's reasonableness.

q: Per Sec. 4.3.2, for what kinds of engagements is Time-Basis compensation typically applied?
o: Services not yet well-defined, pre-design work, partial/additional services, or expert-witness/specialist assignments
n: Time-basis fees suit engagements that are hard to scope in advance or are short/interim in nature — pre-design, partial, additional, expert-witness, and specialist-consultancy work.

q: Per Sec. 4.3.8, to which category of work — and for what reason — is the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense method restricted?
o: All architectural and engineering design work
Non-creative tasks only (accounting, secretarial work, research, report preparation), since creative value can't be fairly measured by hours spent
n: Because creative design value can't be fairly measured by hours spent, this method is restricted to non-creative tasks like accounting, secretarial work, research, and report preparation.

q: Per Sec. 4.3.13, under what condition is a Retainer arrangement used?
o: When services are needed only once, for a single occasion
When services are expected intermittently over a period, for a minimum service obligation
n: A retainer suits clients who want an Architect on-call without full-time engagement — a fixed regular amount for a minimum service obligation, with extra work billed separately.

q: For a Group 2 building (e.g., a school or office building) with a PCC of ₱50.0M or less, what DAEDS RPF applies?
n: Group 2 (moderate-complexity buildings like schools, offices, malls) sits between Group 1 (5%) and Group 3 (7%) at a 6% base DAEDS rate for PCC up to P50M.

q: For a Group 3 building (e.g., a hospital or airport) with a PCC of ₱50.0M or less, what DAEDS RPF applies?
n: Group 3 (hospitals, airports, hotels, and similarly complex facilities) requires the greatest research/engineering input among the three research-heavy groups, hence the highest base DAEDS rate of 7%.

q: Which fee-adjustment factor specifically addresses certification costs for programs such as LEED®, GREEEN®, or BERDE®?
n: Sec. 6.5.4 specifically calls out certification costs for green-building programs like LEED, GREEEN, and BERDE as a fee-adjustment factor.

q: During Jury deliberations in an Architectural Design Competition, what role does the Professional Advisor play?
o: Casts the deciding vote when the Jury is split
Attends the deliberations but does not vote
Chairs the Jury and votes on every entry
Is barred from attending Jury deliberations
n: The Professional Advisor organizes and supervises the competition and assists the Jury during deliberations, but has no vote — the Jurors alone decide.

q: Per Sec. 13.4, how must the ADC Jury be composed?
o: Entirely of lay members representing the Owner
A majority of RLAs, assisted by one lay Juror representing the Owner
Only of the Professional Advisor and Technical Advisors
n: The Jury must be majority RLAs (licensed architects) to ensure technical competence, assisted by one lay Juror who represents the Owner's intentions.

q: In a two-stage design competition, what follows if no contract is signed within twelve months of the Jury's award announcement?
o: The competition is voided and must be re-run
The winner is paid a further sum equal to the first prize
n: This protects the winner's interest if the Owner delays commissioning the project after a two-stage competition — a form of compensation for the extended wait.

q: Per Sec. 14.1.1, how is a "Filipino Professional Consulting Architect" (FPCA) defined?
o: A Filipino citizen who need not be a licensed architect
A Filipino citizen and RLA in good IAPOA standing
n: An FPCA must be both a Filipino citizen and a Registered/Licensed Architect in good standing with IAPOA, specializing in a recognized branch of the profession.

q: Where no qualified FPCA can be found for a specialized consulting engagement, what does Sec. 14.1.1.3 require before a Foreign Consultant may be relied upon?
o: At least two Filipino RLAs must be employed as understudies
Only a Foreign Architect may be hired, with no other condition
The Owner must postpone the project by a full year
n: This safeguard ensures Filipino professionals gain exposure/training on specialized engagements even when no qualified FPCA is on hand, before a Foreign Consultant may otherwise be relied upon.

q: Per Sec. 15, who is barred from lawfully collecting a fee for architectural services?
o: A Construction Manager holding a PCAB license
n: Only those registered/licensed under R.A. 9266 may lawfully collect fees for architectural services — practicing or billing without this standing is unlawful.

q: Per Sec. 17, who shoulders government taxes (such as VAT) levied on the Architect's services for a project?
o: The Architect, deducted from the Professional Fee
The Owner, since the Architect's fee is stated net to the Architect
Architect and Owner in equal shares
n: The Architect's fee is stated as net to the Architect, so any government tax on the services (like VAT), aside from income tax, is passed on to and shouldered by the Owner.

q: For the Sorsogon Medical Center DADS Worksheet (Annex E), starting from the 4.2% Group 3 DADS base and applying the equivalent adjustment factors, what adjusted sub-total fee rate results?
n: DADS starts at a 4.2% base (60% of Group 3's 7.0% DAEDS rate); adding the same-nature adjustment factors (0.30+0.06+0.06+0.06+0.06+0.15 = 0.63%) brings the sub-total to 4.83%.
ref: UAP-IAPOA Doc. 210, Annex E — DADS Worksheet
